data.long_meaning: Emisha is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Emi' (Goddess) and 'Sha' (Apsara). Apsaras are celestial beings, often depicted as beautiful and graceful dancers in Hindu mythology. They are believed to bring happiness and prosperity. The name Emisha carries the meaning “Goddess Apsara” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Emisha usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess apsara and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Emisha or Aemesha was an important goddess of the Vedic religion, mentioned in the Rigveda and the Atharvaveda. She is associated with the creation of the universe and is often described as the mother of the gods and the goddess of nourishment.

Emisha was also revered in medieval India as the goddess of wisdom and learning. She was believed to grant knowledge, remove ignorance, and bestow prosperity upon her devotees. Emisha was especially worshipped by students during their examinations.
